title: Qt: Add Install Plugin to Tools menu
description:
Add an option to the tools menu to copy a binary plugin file
(a .dll or .so) to the personal plugin folder.

This avoids the user having to create the paths manually and
knowning a lot of relatively unimportant details about where and
how Wireshark loads binary plugins.

It will also try to validate the plugin and do some sanity checks to
ensure the ABI is compatible.

notes.body:
added 5 commits
  • 3061bbc3...866de7bc - 4 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 871856ee - Qt: Add Install Plugin to Tools menu
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13582/diffs?diff_id=865677442&start_sha=3061bbc37483bb9889f7625d43c496a65ed6b38b)

If we're not building with plugins, we're not building wiretap/plugins.c, [so `plugins_check_file()` and `plugins_pers_type_folder ()` aren't defined at link time.](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/5699550130)

The code in wireshark_main_window.cpp that does plugin work should perhaps be protected with `#ifdef HAVE_PLUGINS`/`#endif`, and the "Install Plugin" menu item shouldn't be available if we're building without plugin support.

(I'm not sure what the "No options" build is; if it means "don't have any `-D` options when running CMake", I'm not sure why that appears to build without plugins enabled, given that`ENABLE_PLUGINS` defaults to on.... @geraldcombs?)
The "no options job" is intended to catch errors such as these, where the build breaks with something disabled.
QDir and QFile have no error reporting. It's really annoying.

added 12 commits
  • 871856ee...158e1045 - 11 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • c76a28fc - Qt: Add Install Plugin to Tools menu
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/13582/diffs?diff_id=866750981&start_sha=871856eee795ed5ed41b2574b8b70c84bcb54bbb)

> The "no options job" is intended to catch errors such as these, where the build breaks with something disabled.

So "no options" mean "disable everything that defaults to being enabled, and don't enable anything", not "don't pass any command-line configuration options to CMake", i.e. "option" refers to features of Wireshark that can be enabled or disabled.
